thread.title: Markets Now: Dow Tumbles 230 Points as Tech Wreck Spreads

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Markets Now: Dow Tumbles 230 Points as Tech Wreck Spreads
text:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was sitting pretty at the end of January. And then it wasn't, as a correction hit. Since then it's gone up and down and up again, and the wild swings don't seem likely to end any time soon. With that in mind, we're keeping a semi-live look on the volatile markets. Here's the latest from Barron's reporters...
4:15 p.m. Now that the dust has cleared, the The Dow Jones Industrial Average ended down 335.60 points, or 1.35%, to 24610.91, while the S&P 500 lost 39.09 points, or 1.42%, to 2712.92, and the Nasdaq fell 137.74 points, or 1.84%, to 7344.24.
Well off the market's lows. That's something at least.
3:25 p.m. With 35 minutes left in the trading day, the market is off its lows. What happens next could tells us a lot about where it might be headed in the short term. Let's just say we'd like to see the market bounce off its lows even more.
The S&P 500 has dropped 1.7% to 2705.55, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average has fallen 384.56 points, or 1.5%, to 24,561.95. The Nasdaq Composite has tumbled 2.2% to 7319.64.
So we know that Facebook (FB) was the catalyst for today's drop, but the pain has spread well beyond tech. And that's the thing about fragile markets--they don't need a "reason" to drop if they want to go down. Now the market will be looking ahead to the FOMC meeting that begins tomorrow and ends on Wednesday. Will that become just another reason to sell?
10:53 a.m. The stock market is a funny beast. We noted this morning how the Nasdaq Composite was getting hammered after reports of data misuse by a Facebook (FB) customer caused its shares to tumble and the tech sector to fall . But that drop came all at once, and the Nasdaq remains close to where it was before the open: It's down 1.4% at 7376.97.
Illustration: Michael Nagle/Bloomberg But it looks like the jitters that it engendered are spreading more widely, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average has fallen 232.4 points, or 0.9%, to 24,714.09, while the S&P 500 has dropped 0.9% to 2726.37, both worse than when we last checked in on the major averages. As we noted this past weekend, we suspected that the market would retest its correction lows, and that the "reason" if there was one would be different than it was back in February .
Reasons, however, are often just rationalizations for investor behavior. At Friday's close, the S&P 500 was sitting on its 50-day moving average, which had acted as support for three straight days. Today, the index opened will below it. Now it needs to hold support at 2,730, explains Instinet's Frank Cappelleri . "How the index behaves in proximity to that 2,730 zone could be telling for its near-term prospects," he writes.
It doesn't look so good, does it?
7:50 a.m. Call it a tech-trastrope. Yes, all the indexes are down this morning, with S&P 500 futures down 0.6%, and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures off 136 points, or 0.5%. Nasdaq Composite futures, however, have tumbled 1.3%, nearly triple the Dow's loss, thanks to the revelations about the misuse of Facebook (FB) data and its ripple effect through the tech sector.
Illustration: Getty Images That Facebook is down 3.6% at $178.40 shouldn't come as much of a surprise. But most of the other FANGs--and FAANGS, and FAANMGs--are also down solidly as well. Apple (AAPL) has declined 0.6% to $177.00, Netflix (NFLX) has fallen 1.1% to $315.00, Microsoft (MSFT) has slipped 1% to $93.65, and Alphabet (GOOGL) has dropped 1.5% to $1,118. Only Amazon.com (AMZN), up 0.2% at $1,575, is higher.
"This episode appears likely to create another and potentially more serious public relations 'black eye' for the company and could lead to additional regulatory scrutiny," writes Wells Fargo's Peter Stabler, of Facebook.
For the entire industry too, we might add. And given that the market seems to be supported by tech--the best performing sector since the last month's correction--that could men trouble if another sector doesn't pick up the slack.
